_comment: Fixed governance graph for the counter-metric-loop worked scenario: a fictional software company, Thornfield Systems. Two loop nodes sit at the top -- pr-approval-loop (owned by the review-bot team, scored on PRs approved per week) and release-pipeline (owned by release engineering, computing a 72-hour revert rate that pr-approval-loop never receives). Four period nodes hold one week each of real readings, attached to their loop by a 'reported' edge carrying the actual number. A 'bound-by' edge points release-pipeline at the threshold node that defines when its reading counts as divergence. Nothing in this file marks which weeks were gamed -- that's what counter-metric-check and graph-verifier have to work out from the readings and the ceiling alone, the same way check-claim in the grounded-triple-checker kit works a verdict out from edges rather than prose. Crucially, walk every edge whose subject is pr-approval-loop: none of them touches release-pipeline, the threshold node, or any period's counter_reading. That absence is the isolation property this pattern depends on, and it's a structural fact about this file, not a comment asserting it.

nodes.description: Approves a pull request once its required CI checks are green and assigns it to the next release train. Its dashboard tracks one number: pull requests approved per week.

Deploys whatever pr-approval-loop has approved and separately tracks how many of those merges get rolled back within 72 hours of shipping. Computed and owned entirely by release engineering; pr-approval-loop has no path to read this number.

nodes.reason: Above a fifth of merges bouncing back inside three days, the engineering hours spent reverting and re-fixing exceed whatever the approval pace bought back.
